prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Conroe, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1363; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision at the intersection in Conroe, Texas. Do I have your permission to record this conversation?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Can you walk me through what happened leading up to the collision?

A: I was driving through the intersection on a green light. I was going about the speed limit, maybe a little under. Then a car came from my right side and went through the red light.

Q: Did you have any time to react before the impact?

A: Not really. I hit the brakes as soon as I saw the car, but it was too late. It hit the driver's side of my vehicle.

Q: Where did your vehicle end up after the impact?

A: It spun partway around and stopped near the curb on the far side of the intersection. The airbags didn't deploy, but I was thrown against the seat belt pretty hard.

Q: Did you feel any injuries right away?

A: Not at first, I was shaken up. But within a few hours my lower back was really tight and sore. By the next morning I could barely turn to get out of bed.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same day and then I've been seeing my family doctor. They diagnosed a back strain and I've been doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Are you still experiencing pain or limited movement?

A: Yes, the pain comes and goes. Sitting for long periods makes it worse, and I've had to take time off work to get through the appointments.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident?

A: Just that I've been careful and followed the doctor's instructions. I'd like this to be taken care of as quickly as possible.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
